name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
title: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
answer: Data loss prevention and sanitisation in AI security audits covers the controls and processes that keep sensitive data from leaving an organisation through AI tools, prompts, training pipelines, or agent actions. It includes classification of data, monitoring of egress points, and redaction or removal of personal, confidential, regulated, or proprietary content before it reaches a model or vendor. It also covers sanitisation of data used for fine tuning, retrieval, evaluation, and logging, so that residual copies do not become a second leak path. In enterprise enablement, the scope joins policy, procurement, engineering, and user behaviour into one auditable program.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: DLP and sanitisation run on a mix of network and endpoint controls, cloud access security brokers, secure web gateways, API gateways, identity and access management, and data classification platforms. For AI specifically, they sit in front of model APIs, internal model serving layers, vector databases, prompt gateways, and agent tool connectors. Sanitisation services may run as preprocessing jobs, inline filters, or post processing steps that scan outputs for secrets, personal data, or regulated content. Logging and case management systems record alerts, redactions, and exceptions for audit.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Teams map data flows from source systems to AI tools, classify assets, and define rules for what may be sent, stored, or reused. They deploy pattern matching, machine learning classifiers, checksums for secrets, and context rules to detect personal data, credentials, source code, and confidential business information. Sanitisation methods include redaction, masking, tokenisation, pseudonymisation, aggregation, synthetic data generation, and removal of metadata before training or retrieval. Auditors then test the controls with sample prompts, egress attempts, and review of logs to confirm that policies work and exceptions are justified.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: DLP and sanitisation touch privacy rights, contractual confidentiality, trade secrets, intellectual property, data protection obligations, and sector rules. Provenance matters because organisations need to show where training, retrieval, and prompt data came from, what rights attach, and what sanitisation was applied. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how often data and IP disputes surround AI systems. Audit records typically include lawful basis, notices, vendor terms, retention limits, cross border transfers, and incident response. No single control is treated as complete, because risk shifts with new tools, new data sources, and new model behaviour.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: DLP and sanitisation are moving from static rules toward context aware controls that understand prompts, model outputs, and agent behaviour. The direction is toward more inline policy enforcement at the prompt and tool call layer, more automated redaction of retrieval content, and more provenance metadata attached to datasets and model artefacts. Regulation and litigation will keep pressure on enterprises to prove that sensitive data was not used or retained improperly, and the site's 215 compliance and regulation pages reflect that growing body of material. Vendors and open source projects will likely converge on common formats for data classification, consent, and sanitisation logs.
